messages:
maria: heads-up - after landing the kernel-selector change i see p99 go up ~12% on the nv-gpu pool when prefix-prefetch is enabled. traces point to more kernel switching and smaller batches.

sam: do you have a flame/prof? link?

maria: uploading a short snippet from the perf trace

maria: ```
# trace excerpt
batch_size=32 -> effective_tokens_per_batch=210
kernel_selected=conv_fused_v2 -> conv_opt_prefetch
kernel_switches_per_sec=4.8
kv_cache_hit_ratio=0.47
latency_p99=183ms (was 164ms)
```

infra-bot: deploy/green 2065432001 - runtime-kernel-selector v2 rolled to nv-gpu pool :white_check_mark:

eva: hmm. does the kernel selector take into account whether request is prefix-hit vs miss? switching from conv_fused_v2 to conv_opt_prefetch might be cheaper per-token but has worse startup overhead.

sophia: i think our batch formation currently ignores prefix-hit flag. if prefetch hits lead to very short effective decode lengths, the scheduler packs them with misses and forces more frequent kernel transitions.

zach: i saw earlier we have no grouping by "kv_prefix_hit" - everything goes into the same queue. that explains the fragmentation.

maria: exact. the hit-heavy requests have smaller remaining token budgets; they end up creating small micro-batches that cause kernels to thrash.

matt: kernel warmup costs are nontrivial. switching kernels mid-second can cost 10-20ms per switch on these drivers. multiply by 4-5 switches -> p99 delta.

sam: proposal: add a 2-queue admission by hit-ttl: one path for prefix-hit short jobs (fast-kernel affinity) and one for miss/long jobs (quantized-kernel affinity). also increase token_budget_target for the hit queue so it favors grouping hits together.

eva: config sketch:

```yaml
batcher:
  queues:
    - name: hit_fast
      priority: 20
      token_budget_target: 512
      group_by: ["kv_prefix_id", "kernel_affinity"]
    - name: miss_long
      priority: 10
      token_budget_target: 2048
      group_by: ["model_version", "seq_len_bucket"]
  kernel_hysteresis_ms: 40
  min_kernel_hold_ms: 80
```

sophia: love it. also +1 to group_by kernel_affinity so the selector doesn't flip kernels inside a single batch.

zach: wonder if we can do adaptive token_budget_target based on observed hit ratio per-slot. e.g., if hit_ratio>0.6 shrink target for miss queue and grow for hit queue.

matt: caution: dynamic targets can cause oscillation. add dampening (EMA window 30s) and step caps.

sam: experiment plan:
- A: two-queue static targets (hit=512, miss=2048) + kernel_hysteresis
- B: like A but adaptive token targets with EMA(30s)
- measure: p50/p95/p99, kernel_switches/sec, mean_batch_size_by_queue, cost_per_token

maria: i'm happy to run A on nv-gpu pool for 2h peak window tomorrow. will push a small config toggle feature flag.

eva: also add a profiler hook that logs kernel_switch reason and per-batch kernel list. current trace loses reason.

sophia: small perf debug snippet to correlate batch -> kernel list

```json
{
  "batch_id": "b-123",
  "requests": ["r1","r2"],
  "kernel_sequence": ["conv_fused_v2","conv_opt_prefetch"],
  "switch_reasons": ["prefix_hit_affinity","seq_len_mismatch"]
}
```

sam: nice. add a metric: kernel_switches_per_batch and alert if >1% of batches have >1 switch.

maria: assigned: @sam will add metrics/dash, @maria will run A, @sophia will add grouping change, @matt will add hysteresis knobs, @zach will validate no fairness regressions. i'll post results after the run.

sam: should we also pin the kernel selector to prefer the earlier kernel for the first N tokens to avoid micro-warmups? maybe pre-warm on idle.

eva: pre-warm idea is interesting but costy. prefer batching/affinity first.

matt: logging note: include GPU kernel-name in trace to avoid heuristics mismatch.

maria: OK will open a PR with the config and the minimal telemetry diff today. thanks team :thumbsup:

infra-bot: ticket created #INT-8473 "prefetch-aware-batching experiment A" assigned to maria, sam, sophia

maria: will update thread with dashboard link and a short table after the run.
